Over the course of the session, we became familiar with the previous faculty (Malay sir) teaching style, methods of note making, and approach to covering the syllabus. The sudden change of faculty in the middle of the academic session has created a sense of discontinuity in our preparation. With examinations approaching in approximately two months, maintaining consistency in teaching becomes especially crucial. Adjusting to a different teaching methodology at this stage may adversely affect our comprehension, revision strategy, and overall performance.

Moreover, General Studies constitutes a vast and significant portion of our syllabus, and History forms an important foundation for several interconnected topics. Continuity in instruction is therefore essential to ensure effective preparation and optimum academic outcomes.
suggestions: History is often perceived as a vast and demanding subject, yet his unique pedagogical approach transformed it into a subject that students genuinely looked forward to studying. He not only imparted knowledge but also cultivated curiosity and motivation among students, encouraging consistent preparation and deeper understanding. His classes were structured, interactive, and highly beneficial from both conceptual and examination perspectives. Hence we found Malay sir's methodology as the most suitable style and connected with that. It would be highly appreciated if the Management brings him back.
